Toy tip values of a continuous trait

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_tip_values.Rd

Values of a continuous trait for the 30 tips of phylograftR::toy_backbone. They are the data used to build phylograftR::toy_contMap and phylograftR::toy_contMaps, examples of continuous traits discretized into states to constrain the grafting (see phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap()).

They were simulated with phytools::fastBM() under a Brownian Motion (ancestral value of 0 at the root, evolutionary rate sig2 = 1), with seed 37. Among the first 150 seeds, this is one of the seeds for which the discretization of the contMap into three states using the terciles of the tip values gives states that cover similar shares of the branches (35% "low", 43% "medium" and 22% "high"), and constraints that differ among the 7 toy missing taxa of phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list.

Usage

data(toy_tip_values)

Format

A named numeric vector of length 30, named after the tips of phylograftR::toy_backbone and in the same order. The values range from about -7.5 to 4.2.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_contMap for the contMap of this trait (point estimate).

  • phylograftR::toy_contMaps for 10 stochastic histories of this trait (list of contMaps).

  • phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap() to discretize a contMap into a simmap, and phylograftR::convert_values_to_states() to convert continuous values into the same states.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_tip_values)

# Distribution of the values
summary(toy_tip_values)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> -7.5157 -0.2817  0.8178  0.5176  1.7173  4.2193 

# Terciles of the tip values: cut points used to define three states
quantile(toy_tip_values, probs = c(1/3, 2/3))
#>   33.33333%   66.66667% 
#> -0.06642759  1.49246937
